messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online Course: Markov and Hidden Markov Models with Applications in R – 1–4 September
messages.subject_clean: Online Course: Markov and Hidden Markov Models with Applications in R – 1–4 September
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
there are still a few seats for the upcoming online course Markov and Hidden Markov Models with Applications in R, taking place 1?4 September.
 
Course website: [ https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/markov-and-hidden-markov-models-with-applications-in-r/ ]( https://www.physalia-courses.org/courses-workshops/markov-and-hidden-markov-models-with-applications-in-r/ ) 
 
The course provides a practical introduction to Markov and hidden Markov models for longitudinal data, covering model specification, estimation, interpretation, model selection, and applications to continuous and categorical data, including missing values.
 
Participants will gain hands-on experience applying these methods in R using the LMest package, with practical exercises and real-world examples throughout the course.
 R experience: Basic familiarity with R is desirable but not required.
 
The course is suitable for students, researchers, and practitioners in academia, industry, and consultancy who want to learn how to apply Markov and hidden Markov models.
 
 
Best regards,
 
Carlo
 
 

--------------------

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Introduction to GLMM and GAMM with R — Hybrid course
messages.subject_clean: Introduction to GLMM and GAMM with R — Hybrid course
messages.body_plain:
Join Dr Alain F. Zuur and Dr Elena Ieno for a practical five-day 
introduction to generalised linear mixed-effects models and generalised 
additive mixed models in R.

Topics include random intercepts and slopes, nested models, GLMMs, 
nonlinear relationships, hierarchical GAMs, model selection and 
validation. Examples cover continuous, count, binary and proportional 
data, primarily using glmmTMB and mgcv.

Dates: 17?21 August 2026, 09:00?16:00 (Dutch time)
Location: Brightlands Campus Venlo, the Netherlands, or online via Zoom
Course fee: ?500, including 12 months? access to the course website and 
a one-hour consultation about your own data. All exercises and theory 
presentations are also available as on-demand video.

Flyer: 
https://www.highstat.com/Courses/Flyers/Flyer2026_08_Maastricht_GLMMGAMM.pdf

Information and registration: 
https://www.highstat.com/index.php/joine-an-onsite-course

Kind regards,

Alain Zuur

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] SEM and Multilevel Models in R and Mplus with AI - livestream seminar
messages.subject_clean: SEM and Multilevel Models in R and Mplus with AI - livestream seminar
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone

Instats is excited to offer a 2-day seminar, SEM in R and Mplus with AI <https://instats.org/seminar/sem-in-r-and-mplus-with-ai>, running August 13?14. This practice-oriented workshop introduces structural equation modeling for researchers who want to move confidently from regression-based approaches to latent variable modeling in Mplus and R using lavaan. A distinctive feature of the seminar is its integration of generative AI tools, including Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot, to support SEM coding, troubleshooting, interpretation, and reproducible research workflows in a transparent and methodologically responsible way. 

The seminar is part of a 2-part sereies on SEM and Multilevel Models in R and Mplus with AI <https://instats.org/course/sem-and-multilevel-models-in-r-and-mplus1>, with the multilevel modeling seminar running August 20?21. By purchasing both seminars, participants save 10% on their regular price. After completing the full course, you will have a full understanding of how to model complex datasets that involve multiple variables at multilevel levels of analysis ? including Multilevel SEM applications in R and Mplus.

Sign up today <https://instats.org/course/sem-and-multilevel-models-in-r-and-mplus1> to secure your spot, and feel free to share this opportunity with colleagues and students who might benefit!


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
Institute for Statistical and Data Science

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online course: Causal Roadmaps for Ecology
messages.subject_clean: Online course: Causal Roadmaps for Ecology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

A reminder - Clarify ecological comparisons before translating field and monitoring data into estimates. Data Can Deceive: Causal Roadmaps is a seminar livestreaming August 5 with Robert Platt (School of Population and Global Health, McGill University), Kathryn Morrison (Precision Analytics), and Andy Wilson (Spencer Fox Eccles School of Medicine, University of Utah). Formulate causal estimands, map assumptions with directed acyclic graphs, and build target-trial protocols for observational ecological studies. Apply these tools to vegetation, soil, hydrology, or other environmental data in R by aligning eligibility, time zero, exposures, and outcomes. Evaluate confounding and inappropriate adjustment, then document analytic decisions so collaborators can audit the resulting causal claim.

Details and registration: https://instats.org/seminar/data-can-deceive-causal-roadmaps
Further information is available on the seminar page.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Handle species occurrence data in R (live online course)
messages.subject_clean: Handle species occurrence data in R (live online course)
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,

Transmitting Science is offering the course "Species occurrence data 
download and cleaning with R" (8th edition).

Course webpage: 
https://www.transmittingscience.com/courses/ecology/species-occurrence-data-download-and-cleaning-with-r

Species occurrence data are essential for a range of ecological and 
biogeographical analyses. Although they are now widely available in 
multiple online sources, they are heterogeneous and come with caveats 
that need to be addressed before moving on with the analysis.

In this short course, we will use a range of tools to:
*    Import species occurrence data from various sources into R (e.g. 
GBIF, iNaturalist, VertNet, EcoEngine)
*    Join and arrange these data into a homogeneous dataset for analysis
*    Map and visually inspect the data for taxonomic and spatial errors 
and bias
*    Clean the data by removing detectable errors
*    Correct or minimise spatial bias

The course will be highly interactive and will include both theoretical 
and practical sessions. Participants are encouraged to work with their 
own species of interest, although several illustrative examples will 
also be provided.

For any questions, please write to courses at transmittingscience.com
Best regards,

Haris

-- 
Haris Saslis, PhD
Course Coordinator
Transmitting Science

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online course: Social Network Analysis with ERGM
messages.subject_clean: Online course: Social Network Analysis with ERGM
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

Network methods offer a useful lens on relationships within ecological systems. Social Network Analysis: From Basics to ERGM led by Antonio Zinilli (Research Institute on Sustainable Economic Growth, National Research Council of Italy (CNR)) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. Prepare network data in R, create informative visualisations, calculate centrality measures, and identify communities in ecological relationship data. Fit and diagnose exponential random graph models to examine network structure and test research questions. Ecologists can apply these techniques to connections among species, sites, organisations, or environmental processes in their own studies.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/social-network-analysis-from-basics-to-e-1
Please circulate this information if it is relevant to colleagues or students.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
Instats | instats.org

Dear all,
Are you ready to take your R skills beyond the basics?
 
Join our online workshop, Beyond Beginner R: Advancing Your Coding Skills, taking place 27?30 October.
 
Designed for researchers with working knowledge of R, this four-day course focuses on building clean, reproducible, collaborative, and maintainable R workflows.
 
You will learn to:
Write advanced and reusable R code using the tidyverse, functions, and purrr
Build reproducible projects and reports with Quarto
Create publication-quality visualisations with ggplot2
Collaborate and manage code with GitHub
Use AI coding assistants critically and effectively, including code validation and agentic workflows
? 13:00?19:00 Berlin time | Online

messages.subject: [R-sig-eco] Online course: QGIS spatial data ecology
messages.subject_clean: Online course: QGIS spatial data ecology
messages.body_plain:
Hello R-SIG-ECOLOGY members

Ecological datasets often reveal additional questions when their spatial structure is made visible. Introduction to QGIS & Spatial Data led by Nick Bearman (University College London and Geospatial Training Solutions) is now available as an on-demand streaming seminar. QGIS techniques for loading vector and raster data, conducting joins, and calculating fields can support ecological spatial analysis. Learn data classification, preparation, map styling, and publication-ready layout design for environmental evidence. Apply these methods to vegetation, soils, hydrology, or other ecological datasets when communicating spatial research findings.

Course details: https://instats.org/seminar/introduction-to-qgis-and-spatial-data-1
The course page includes the curriculum and enrollment details.


Best wishes

Michael Zyphur
Professor and Director
